hints: Notice sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave made by vibrating air particles, so think what it needs to travel.
Recall that only transverse waves with vibrations across the direction of travel can be polarised.
Recall that diffraction through a gap is shown by all types of waves when gap width is similar to wavelength.
walkthrough: Identify sound as a longitudinal progressive wave where air particles oscillate parallel to the direction of energy transfer.
For vacuum travel: a longitudinal sound wave needs a material medium to compress and rarefy, so in a vacuum with no particles it cannot travel - first entry is no.
For polarisation: polarisation restricts transverse vibrations to one plane, but a longitudinal wave has only one vibration direction along travel, so sound cannot be polarised - second entry is no.
For diffraction: all waves spread out after passing through a gap of similar size to their wavelength, and sound is heard around doorways, so sound can diffract - third entry is yes.
The combination no, no, yes matches the table row. This is option A.

options.A: Sound needs a medium, is longitudinal so cannot be polarised, but like all waves it can diffract.
options.B: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because it needs particles to vibrate, and it can diffract through a gap.
options.C: Sound is longitudinal with vibrations parallel to travel, so it cannot be polarised and it does diffract.
options.D: Although sound cannot travel in a vacuum and can diffract, it cannot be polarised because it is not transverse.
